intelligence.human_view: A summary is not a step toward done — it is a redo he has to do himself. That is the whole law in one line. Eight or nine summaries mean he has to go put the right stuff in eight or nine times: the machine did the easy shape of the work and handed him the hard part — the actual words, the actual decisions — eight or nine times over. A prototype is the same debt in a different shape: something that looks like progress and isn't, because it was never meant to be the thing. We are professionals, and professionalism is not a tone, it is a standard: go all in, do things right, ready to go, completed and done. The legal pages are the proof of the cost — round 1 built summaries (58 boards) and called it the pages, and now the writer has to draft all eight properly (74 sections, ~6,600 words), he has to give the text on the four rulings only he can make, and the builder has to create the pages extraordinary — the whole job, again, because the first pass was a summary instead of the work. Do it right the first time and none of that repeats: the work arrives complete, he reads it, he rules on the parts only he can rule on, and it ships.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine your teacher asks you to write a story, and you just write one tiny sentence about it instead of the whole story! Then the teacher has to go and write the whole story herself — eight or nine times! That's not helping at all! The rule now is: do the WHOLE job, properly, the first time — no tiny summaries, no pretend versions! Be a professional: finish it for real, so nobody has to do it again!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine you ask someone to bake you a cake, dear, and they bring you a little drawing of a cake and say "here's a summary of the cake"! You'd still have to go and bake the cake yourself, love — eight or nine times if they drew eight or nine cakes! What good is the drawing? The rule now, dear: do it right the first time. No summaries, no pretend versions — go all in, do it properly, ready to go, completed and done, so he never has to put the right stuff in again and again. A professional finishes the job, love — they don't hand you the homework.
